alerts.title: Red Sea Rerouting Adds Days to Transit Times
alerts.summary: Vessels continue rerouting around the Cape of Good Hope due to Red Sea security risks, significantly extending east-west transit times. Drewry's container rate index has climbed to its highest level since September 2024 as a result.

alerts.title: Global Port Congestion Hits 4-Year High
alerts.summary: Over 10% of the global container fleet is waiting at anchorage, with 80% of 454 tracked ports experiencing elevated congestion. Average vessel wait times range from near zero at efficient hubs to over 45 days at the worst-affected ports.

alerts.title: Shanghai, Ningbo, Rotterdam Face Multi-Week Delays
alerts.summary: Severe congestion at Shanghai, Ningbo, Rotterdam, and Antwerp is creating cascading delays across east-west trade lanes, compounded by Typhoon SAUDEL which closed Ningbo for 78 hours this week. Carriers are skipping ports and omitting calls to recover schedules, raising rollover risk for general cargo bookings.

alerts.title: US to Prohibit Certain Canadian Imports from Sep 29
alerts.summary: The Trump Administration has announced a prohibition on importation of certain Canadian products effective September 29, 2026, escalating the ongoing US-Canada trade dispute. This follows Canada's September 8 retaliatory tariffs on US steel and electronics and is expected to further disrupt North American supply chains.

alerts.title: Copper Output Falls at Codelco and Freeport
alerts.summary: Copper futures fell nearly 5% in a single session before stabilizing near $6.45/lb, pressured by US reconsideration of refined metal import tariffs. Major miners Codelco and Freeport-McMoRan reported double-digit production declines, contributing to a 1.1% drop in global copper output in H1 2026.

alerts.title: Typhoon SAUDEL Closes Ningbo, Disrupts Asia Schedules
alerts.summary: Typhoon SAUDEL forced the closure of Ningbo port for 78 hours this week and is driving vessel bunching across Asia, extending the US peak shipping season into September. The National Retail Federation forecasts 2.31 million TEUs will move through major US ports in September, potentially the busiest month of 2026.

alerts.title: Crude Oil Hits $100/bbl as Iran-Gulf Hormuz Talks Open
alerts.summary: Brent crude reached $99.99/barrel on September 11, up 20% over the past month and 59.5% year-on-year, driven by Middle East tensions and supply constraints. Iranian state media confirmed Tehran will meet Gulf states in Oman to discuss the Strait of Hormuz, introducing uncertainty into the key oil transit chokepoint.

alerts.title: Canada Hits US Steel and Electronics with Tariffs
alerts.summary: Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs on US steel, electronics, and other products starting September 8, responding to Washington's 50% levy on $20 billion in Canadian goods. US-Canada trade negotiations remain stalled, with Trump warning of further escalation.

alerts.title: US Treasury Broadens Iran Aviation Sanctions
alerts.summary: The US Treasury Department has expanded Iran aviation sanctions, increasing scrutiny of regional support networks and raising compliance risks for MRO companies, freight forwarders, aircraft brokers, and parts suppliers in the UAE, Turkey, Malaysia, and other transit markets. Companies with exposure to these networks face heightened enforcement risk.

alerts.title: Port Klang Emergency Dredging Sep 7-27 Limits Drafts
alerts.summary: Emergency maintenance dredging at Port Klang, Malaysia from September 7 to 27 is restricting vessel drafts and complicating schedules for Southeast Asia-bound cargo. The timing coincides with peak typhoon-season disruptions across Asia, increasing cumulative schedule pressure.

alerts.title: Panama Canal Re-Imposes Draft Restrictions in 2026
alerts.summary: The Panama Canal Authority has reintroduced vessel draft restrictions in 2026 as water levels remain below historical norms following the severe 2023-2024 drought. Shippers on trans-Pacific and US East Coast lanes face reduced cargo loads per transit, adding cost and pushing some volume to alternative routes.

alerts.title: Pointe Noire Port Yard Over Capacity, 3+ Day Delays
alerts.summary: Pointe Noire (Republic of the Congo) is experiencing severe yard congestion exceeding 100% utilization, with vessel waiting times reaching 3.4 days and vessel delays of up to five days. The congestion is disrupting cargo flows for West and Central African importers relying on this key gateway.

alerts.title: US Pax Silica Initiative Reshaping Semiconductor Supply
alerts.summary: A new US-led economic cooperation framework called Pax Silica is pulling allied nations into coordinated semiconductor and AI hardware supply chain blocs, accelerating decoupling from Chinese supply networks. Companies dependent on Chinese chip packaging, advanced substrates, or rare earth inputs face growing sourcing disruption risk as the initiative takes hold.

alerts.title: Pre-National Day Cargo Surge to Intensify Sep Congestion
alerts.summary: Shippers are accelerating bookings ahead of China's National Day Golden Week holiday (October 1), compounding congestion caused by typhoon-delayed cargo competing for limited capacity. Carriers have pulled approximately 20% of capacity via blank sailings, pushing FAK bookings into elevated rollover risk through end of September.

disruptionZones.desc: Ongoing security threats forcing vessels to reroute around Cape of Good Hope, adding 10-14 days to Asia-Europe transit times and driving container rates to multi-year highs.

Three typhoons in five weeks, including SAUDEL closing Ningbo for 78 hours, driving vessel bunching across Asia; pre-National Day cargo rush at end of September expected to intensify congestion further.

US-Canada trade war escalating: Canada imposed Sep 8 retaliatory tariffs on US steel and electronics; US import prohibition on certain Canadian goods effective Sep 29; Panama Canal draft restrictions adding further transit cost.
Iran-Gulf state talks in Oman over Strait of Hormuz access introduce uncertainty; ~20% of global oil trade transits this chokepoint daily.
Rotterdam and Antwerp experiencing cascading delays as late-arriving vessels from Asia create uneven cargo surges and operational inefficiencies.
